variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A WhatsApp-style messaging system is a private, real-time delivery network that accepts a message from one device, routes encrypted copies to the recipient's devices, and keeps retrying safely when a device is offline or an acknowledgement is lost.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Accept once, attempt at least once, display once”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Name and encrypt
pairs.detail: Reuse one client message ID across sender retries, resolve each recipient device session, and create authenticated ciphertext locally.
pairs.explanation: Reuse one client message ID across sender retries, resolve each recipient device session, and create authenticated ciphertext locally.

pairs.label: Authorize and commit
pairs.detail: Check membership and idempotency, assign conversation order, and atomically commit the message record plus per-device outbox events.
pairs.explanation: Check membership and idempotency, assign conversation order, and atomically commit the message record plus per-device outbox events.

pairs.label: Push or retain
pairs.detail: Push online device envelopes, retain offline work with expiry, and schedule bounded retries using the same identity.
pairs.explanation: Push online device envelopes, retain offline work with expiry, and schedule bounded retries using the same identity.

pairs.label: Persist and acknowledge
pairs.detail: Authenticate and decrypt, store the message and seen ID together, then acknowledge only that device's queue item.
pairs.explanation: Authenticate and decrypt, store the message and seen ID together, then acknowledge only that device's queue item.

variants.context: A WhatsApp-style messaging system is a private, real-time delivery network that accepts a message from one device, routes encrypted copies to the recipient's devices, and keeps retrying safely when a device is offline or an acknowledgement is lost.
variants.prompt: What is the core delivery invariant in this design?
options: One logical message ID can have independent encrypted delivery state per recipient device
Every recipient device must join the sender's database transaction
A retry always receives a new message ID
The routing service must hold the recipient's content keys
variants.explanation: Stable logical identity prevents duplicate display, while per-device state lets each phone, tablet, web, or desktop session progress independently.
